items.summary: Security disposition: evidence_needed. Exact decision: keep new public exposure and security-sensitive releases gated; permit ordinary reversible growth only within existing consent, disclosure, data-handling, dependency, permission, and rollback boundaries. Evidence: security baseline generated 2026-09-30T22:50:04.738Z reports fleet-doctor unavailable with no run, findings, or site checks across 61 managed sites; operations deploy, uptime, and error sweeps have no results. Authentication boundaries, secrets handling, container isolation, release/deploy controls, dependency provenance, monitoring, incident readiness, and security.txt/disclosure readiness are therefore unevidenced. No TLS certificates are reported expiring within 30 days, but complete TLS posture is unknown. Compliance reports 36 pass, 19 fail, and 6 unknown; this is a technical baseline, not certification, and includes consent/banner/GA4 and privacy/terms failures. Risk severity: high for public launch or security-sensitive release due to control-evidence gaps; medium for bounded reversible growth that adds no credentials, permissions, dependencies, data collection, or cross-site behavior. Do not claim certification or a clean bill of health. Do not retrieve credentials, access private containers, exploit targets, modify permissions/configuration, deploy, add dependencies, or request duplicate telemetry.

Security handoff: complete the existing fleet security evidence matrix using authorized metadata and retained artifacts only. Record dated evidence, affected scope, owners, severity, and release implications for authentication/access boundaries, secrets exposure, runtime isolation, release and deployment controls, dependency and supply-chain provenance, TLS, data exposure, monitoring and incident signals, and security.txt/disclosure readiness. Preserve all existing launch and security-sensitive release gates until evidence supports an owner-approved disposition.
